issues: FIDELITY FAIL — assembled_top.png (the canonical top-down render) shows the knob's finger-scalloped top face and its ring of ~12 grip dots plainly visible through/above `knob_hood`, directly contradicting brief §4.1-4.2 ("the hood must hide the setter's hand... the direction of every turn") and §9's abort-on-sight rule. DEVIATIONS.md D4 changed the hood roof from a flat cap to a 45° cone narrowing to ⌀47.6 at the top for print-support reasons but records no re-check of that opening against the hidden-state requirement the flat top was originally there to satisfy. This is the Armillary-class defect named in the review brief: hidden state visible in a render is FAIL-grade regardless of geometric intent. Disposition: repair — either cap the cone's top or prove (with a corrected render) that the ⌀47.6 opening does not expose the knob.

SELLABILITY note — 42 printed parts / 34.5h build vs the stated 6-20 part / ≤20h guideline. This is not build-time drift: it matches brief §8's own disclosed number and its recommendation to price at $79 or not at all. Disposition: brief-defect / arbitration (price point and 0.7 units/machine-day throughput), not a CAD finding.

PRINTABILITY — no findings. All running/sliding fit clearances are ≥0.15 mm; the only sub-0.15 mm values are intentional press/snap interferences (post_guide 0.10, detent_leaf 0.10). Each of the 12 registered deviations (D1-D12) resolves a real print-process or brief-internal conflict with arithmetic shown, including D3 which catches a brief bug that would have jammed the yoke at click 12 of 31.

survives_as_cardboard reasoning: the game's only secret is the felt/heard direction of a hidden hand turn plus a physical detent that makes each click undisputable — a cardboard version has no way to generate or enforce that hidden turn or click without a human acting as a trusted referee, so it does not survive as cardboard.
